source: MAFF/partner document, "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop), Section II: Value/uses of corn -- 1. Corn as human food
text:
Corn is an important crop for both human and livestock benefit. A given quantity of corn contains roughly: 10.8% moisture, 10% protein, 4.3% fat, 73.4% carbohydrate, and 1.4% fiber, among other nutrients.

Corn is eaten as a daily staple food in some countries. In Cambodia it is more often a supplementary food alongside the rice-based staple diet -- people commonly boil, roast/grill, or steam it, and also mix corn into cooked rice (rice with corn). Sweet corn, whose origin traces to America, is typically eaten fresh once the ear is fully filled out, or used in various mixed dishes/salads; this type turns a distinctive red-brown color when ripe.

Based on trends in corn production, corn is expected to become an increasingly major staple crop worldwide -- the document projects that from the year 2000 onward corn could become the number one crop globally. It notes that in 1996, Cambodia's own corn production had already risen to about 63.5 thousand tons.
